subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Sore throat for 4 days
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 45 years old and female. I'm here because I've had a sore throat for about four days, and I think I had a fever last night. I was really sweaty, but I didn't check my temperature because I was already in bed. It's been hard to swallow, and I've been drinking mostly water, though I had some wine at night. Doctor: Could you please confirm your age, gender, and the duration and severity of your sore throat? Have you noticed any other symptoms such as cough, runny nose, or difficulty breathing? Patient: I'm 45 and female. My sore throat has been going on for about four days, and it's really bad—every time I swallow, it hurts, and it's even hard to eat. I haven't had a cough, but I do have a stuffy nose, and I was having chills and a lot of sweating last night. I didn't check my temperature, though. Doctor: Have you experienced any recent travel, close contact with individuals who have infectious diseases, or exposure to sick individuals? Patient: No, I haven't traveled recently, and I don't think I've been in close contact with anyone who's sick. My kids go to school, and they always have little colds or coughs, but nobody else in the house is really complaining of anything. Doctor: Could you please describe whether your sore throat is on one side (unilateral) or both sides (bilateral), and whether you notice any white patches or pus on your tonsils? Patient: It's on both sides, and I think my tonsils are swollen. I don't know if there's white stuff on them, but I do notice some kind of discharge when I look in the mirror. Doctor: Could you please describe the appearance of your tonsils in more detail? Specifically, are there any white patches, redness, or swelling
